key_insight: Underwater C3-JEPA learns a predictive world model for ROV salvage by fusing synchronized multi-view video and control inputs, allowing it to anticipate object state changes even without contact sensors. Its key breakthrough is object-centric, cross-view latent prediction under underwater motion delay and contact interaction.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the challenge of understanding and predicting heavy-load underwater ROV salvage dynamics in near-field operations, where direct contact sensing is unavailable and vehicle motion is affected by hydrodynamic lag.
method: Encodes synchronized multi-camera RGB observations into an object-centric latent representation.
Conditions predictions on vehicle control signals to model how task-object state evolves over time.
Uses cross-view and context-extended predictive learning (C3-JEPA) to infer latent future states during contact and delayed underwater interactions.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this shows how self-supervised world models can support robust robotic decision-making in sensor-limited, real-world environments. It is especially relevant for underwater robotics, manipulation, and predictive control without explicit force/contact sensing.
visual_elements: Multi-camera underwater ROV diagram showing synchronized viewpoints around the target object
Latent world-model pipeline: RGB inputs + control signals -> object-centric encoder -> future state predictor
Before/after sequence illustrating predicted object motion under contact and hydrodynamic lag
Concept icons for cameras, control commands, latent space, and underwater salvage
paper_title: Underwater C3-JEPA: An Object-Centric Cross-View World Model for ROV Salvage
paper_authors: Yuncong Yang, Jinlong Li, Yulong Xue, Feng Wu, Chunwen Zhang
